validator.source_text:
<scxml xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/07/scxml" version="1.0" datamodel="ecmascript" initial="a">
  <datamodel><data id="x" expr="0"/><data id="o" expr="({})"/></datamodel>
  <state id="a">
    <transition event="e1" cond="x ? 1" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e2" cond="x + 1 = 2" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e3" cond="o.a.b = 3" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e4" cond="x.1" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e5" cond="let y = 1" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e6" cond="function() {}" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e7" cond="x in" target="b"/>
    <transition event="e8" cond="'unterminated" target="b"/>
  </state>
  <final id="b"/>
</scxml>

diagnostics.message: ecmascript syntax error in `cond`: the expression ends before it is complete
notes: a condition that cannot be parsed raises `error.execution` and evaluates as false, so this condition can never hold
diagnostics.help: a `?` conditional needs both branches: `test ? whenTrue : whenFalse`

diagnostics.message: ecmascript syntax error in `cond`: the left side of `=` cannot be assigned to
notes: a condition that cannot be parsed raises `error.execution` and evaluates as false, so this condition can never hold
diagnostics.help: `=` assigns, and only a variable or a property such as `a.b` or `a[0]` can be assigned; to compare, write `===` (or `==`)

notes: SCXML 1.0 §5.9.1: "Conditional expressions in conformant SCXML documents SHOULD NOT have side effects." (Appendix B's "This language MUST not have side effects" contradicts official IRP test 444, `cond="++var1==2"`; see docs/spec-errata.md)
diagnostics.help: to compare, use `===` (or `==`); to change the value, move the assignment into `<assign>` in the transition

diagnostics.message: ecmascript syntax error in `cond`: `.1` is not a property access
notes: a condition that cannot be parsed raises `error.execution` and evaluates as false, so this condition can never hold
diagnostics.help: a property name cannot start with a digit; index with brackets: `[1]`

diagnostics.message: ecmascript syntax error in `cond`: `let` declares a variable, which a `cond` cannot do
notes: a condition that cannot be parsed raises `error.execution` and evaluates as false, so this condition can never hold
diagnostics.help: a `cond` must be an expression: declare the variable with `<data id="y" expr="…"/>` in the `<datamodel>`, or set it with `<assign location="y" expr="…"/>`

diagnostics.message: ecmascript syntax error in `cond`: the expression ends before it is complete
notes: a condition that cannot be parsed raises `error.execution` and evaluates as false, so this condition can never hold
diagnostics.help: add the missing operand, closing bracket, or closing quote at the end

diagnostics.message: ecmascript syntax error in `cond`: unterminated string literal
notes: a condition that cannot be parsed raises `error.execution` and evaluates as false, so this condition can never hold
diagnostics.help: close the string with a matching `'`; to include a `'` inside it, escape it as `\'`
